evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The entry says Shuowen’s form for 票 was 𤐫, glossed 火飛也 (“fire flying”), and records that the lower 火 became 示 through clerical transformation. It separately cites Han shu uses for shaking and light movement, and later examples for paper money and documentary credentials. Those later senses are listed with their own citations; the entry does not establish a direct semantic chain from fire to tickets.
evidence.title: [A02895] 票 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 形義通解; 字形資料
evidence.text: The account identifies 𤐫 as an earlier written form of 票, with upper [𦥑囟] and lower 火; it says the upper part was reduced to 覀 and 火 was confused with 示 in the clerical form. Its displayed inventory has one small-seal example and five bamboo-slip examples, but no oracle-bone or bronze examples. This does not prove that earlier attestations do not exist.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 票

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry cites Han shu passages and Tang commentator Yan Shigu for senses involving shaking and light movement, and a Qing salt-administration example for a documentary 引票. It gives paper-money examples from Qing or later literature and cites 車票, 門票, and 選票 as modern examples without dating their first occurrence. This is lexical evidence, not a documented continuous semantic path.
evidence.title: [A02895] 票 - Ministry of Education Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry reports a Shuihudi Qin 日書甲種 slip 57 example 票風, interpreted as a rapid or strong wind, and cites Han shu motion/rapidity examples. It also gives Ming-period examples of 票 used for documentary credentials and later banknotes. The entry reports the Qin-slip reading; the disputed separate phrase 票行 is not used as secure corroboration here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 票

evidence.source: 葛希谷, Fudan University Center for Excavated Texts and Paleography
evidence.field: 論證：睡虎地秦墓竹簡《日書》甲種《盜者》篇“票行”
evidence.text: The author surveys competing readings of a Shuihudi 日書 phrase 票行 and argues that 票 should be read 少, citing a parallel Han-period slip and phonetic-loan examples. This dispute concerns that phrase only and does not disprove other independently supported uses of 票.
evidence.title: 葛希谷：也說睡虎地秦墓竹簡《日書》甲種《盜者》篇的“票行”

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry transcribes Shuowen’s analysis of 𤐫 as 火 plus [𦥑囟] and reports the reading 方昭切. It does not identify the upper graphic element as a particular object or establish a phonetic role for either visible part in 票. Its analysis is a source’s account, not independent proof of the depicted referent.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 票

search_audit.outcome: The exact page establishes the candidate filename and public-domain release, but the requested image URL had already returned 404 and the attempted alternate direct/redirect URLs were inaccessible. No glyph is proposed.

gaps: The upper element [𦥑囟] is not independently identified as a particular depicted object or action. The dossier’s paired-hands/bag/basket and sparks explanations are not established by the inspected references.

No sound component is established by the inspected sources. The local modern reading and Baxter–Sagart reading of 票 do not establish any component’s phonetic role; no component-to-character sound comparison is asserted.
No securely verified oracle-bone or bronze attestation for 票/𤐫 was established. The CUHK entry’s displayed inventory includes seal and bamboo-slip examples but no oracle-bone or bronze examples.

The fire-to-light-movement/rapidity link is an account supported by dictionary citations, but a securely demonstrated dated semantic chain was not found. The Qin-slip 票風 reading is reported by CUHK; 票行 remains disputed.

A secure early attestation for ticket, ballot, or paper credential was not found. The inspected dictionaries give Ming-era documentary examples and Qing-or-later paper-money examples; these do not establish the earliest use of modern ticket senses.
The official Unicode character-specific Unihan endpoint was inaccessible. A search/help page was inspected, and supplied local rows are reported as local data only.

The exact Commons description page was inspected, but its linked image candidate URL returned 404 in acquisition and alternate direct/redirect attempts were inaccessible. No usable alternate image source with verified identity and reuse rights was established, so no glyph image is proposed.
No repeated-source reuse assessment or extract recommendation was made; evidence is limited to character-specific paraphrase.

limitations.text: The Commons file page identifies a modern public-domain seal-script redraw, but its image URL failed acquisition with 404 and attempted alternatives were inaccessible. Xiaoxuetang returned 401 in the supplied query, and no other candidate with verified direct image access and rights was established; therefore no image is proposed.
